evidence: Liv. praef. 3: in tantā scrīptōrum turbā
terms.comment: One who composes in writing, the word’s ruling sense (Lewis & Short); with a genitive, the author of a kind of work: rērum scrīptōrēs, historians (Liv. 21.1.1). Traupman gives scrīptrīx for a woman writer (p. 170).

terms.grammar: noun, third declension, masculine or feminine
terms.gloss: the author of a work; an authority one reads and cites
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.18.1: quōs nunc lēctitō auctōrēs
Suet. Jul. 56: Bellī Alexandrīnī Āfricīque et Hispāniēnsis incertus auctor est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The one a work comes from, and so one whose word counts; also the author of a plan or a deed. Lewis & Short makes it common gender; Traupman’s auctrīx (p. 275) is rare and post-classical (Lewis & Short s.v. auctrīx).

phrases.latin: et sī in tantā scrīptōrum turbā mea fāma in obscūrō sit, nōbilitāte ac magnitūdine eōrum mē, quī nōminī officient meō, cōnsōler
phrases.english: and if, in so great a crowd of writers, my own fame should stay in the shade, I shall console myself with the distinction and greatness of those who will eclipse my name

phrases.latin: habeō nōn nūllōs ex iīs quōs nunc lēctitō auctōrēs quī dīcant fierī id oportēre
phrases.english: I have several among the authors I am reading now who say that this ought to be done
